1: //! The Qt renderer: shared decode core (`RenderTree`) + a sent-state cache
2: //! that produces the delta command batch handed to the C++ Qt layer.
3: //!
4: //! The engine emits diffs, and this renderer forwards diffs: it keeps a mirror
5: //! of what the C++ layer already has (`sent`) and, per frame, emits only the
6: //! commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero** commands. The C++
7: //! layer stays dumb (applies the batch, resets to renderer defaults on
8: //! `RESET_NODE`).
9: 
10: use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
11: 
12: use pathland_core::{value_type, Frame};
13: use pathland_render_core::{HostNode, RenderTree};
14: 
15: use crate::ffi::Command;

17: /// Mirror of the C++ layer's state for one node.
18: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
19: struct SentNode {
20:     text: Option<String>,
21:     props: HashMap<u16, u32>,
22:     strings: HashMap<u16, String>,
23:     date: Option<(i32, u32)>,
24: }
25: 
26: /// Pseudo-parent for tree roots: id `0` maps to the Qt window's contentItem.
27: pub const CONTENT_ITEM: u32 = 0;
28: 
29: /// The retained Qt renderer. Owns the decoded tree (shared core) and the
30: /// sent-state cache used to produce deltas.
31: pub struct QtRenderer {
32:     tree: RenderTree,
33:     sent: HashMap<u32, SentNode>,
34:     sent_children: HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>>,
35: }
36: 
37: impl Default for QtRenderer {
38:     fn default() -> Self {
39:         Self::new()
40:     }
41: }

43: impl QtRenderer {
44:     pub fn new() -> Self {
45:         Self {
46:             tree: RenderTree::default(),
47:             sent: HashMap::new(),
48:             sent_children: HashMap::new(),
49:         }
50:     }
51: 
52:     /// The decoded tree (shared renderer core).
53:     pub fn tree(&self) -> &RenderTree {
54:         &self.tree
55:     }
56: 
57:     /// Set the effective color scheme (renderer-derived, never carried by the
58:     /// protocol) and re-resolve every design token — re-emitting the changed
59:     /// nodes' concrete values to the C++ layer.
60:     pub fn set_scheme(&mut self, scheme: pathland_core::tokens::Scheme) {
61:         self.tree.set_scheme(scheme);
62:         let cmds = self.diff();
63:         crate::ffi::apply(&cmds);
64:     }
65: 
66:     /// Apply one opcode frame and forward the resulting delta batch to the
67:     /// C++ layer. Unchanged nodes produce no commands.
68:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
69:         self.tree.apply_frame(frame);
70:         let cmds = self.diff();
71:         crate::ffi::apply(&cmds);
72:     }
73: 
74:     /// Clear the whole scene (`META::RESET`): empty the tree and tell the C++
75:     /// layer to drop every widget.
76:     pub fn reset(&mut self) {
77:         self.tree = RenderTree::default();
78:         self.sent.clear();
79:         self.sent_children.clear();
80:         unsafe { crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_reset() };
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Compute the delta batch vs the sent-state cache.
84:     ///
85:     /// Commands with strings point into `self.tree`'s owned strings; the
86:     /// returned batch is only valid while `self` is not mutated — callers must
87:     /// forward it immediately (as [`Self::apply_frame`] does).
88:     pub fn diff(&mut self) -> Vec<Command> {
89:         let mut cmds = Vec::new();
90: 
91:         // 1. Deletions first: nodes gone from the tree.
92:         let live: HashSet<u32> = self.tree.nodes.keys().copied().collect();
93:         let dead: Vec<u32> = self
94:             .sent
95:             .keys()
96:             .copied()
97:             .filter(|id| !live.contains(id))
98:             .collect();
99:         for id in dead {
100:             cmds.push(Command::delete_node(id));
101:             self.sent.remove(&id);
102:             self.sent_children.remove(&id);
103:         }
104: 
105:         // 2. Creates (pre-order, so a parent exists before its children are
106:         //    inserted, and a child before any insert references it).
107:         let order = self.pre_order();
108:         for &id in &order {
109:             if self.sent.contains_key(&id) {
110:                 continue;
111:             }
112:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
113:             cmds.push(Command::create_node(id, node.component_type));
114:             self.sent.insert(id, SentNode::default());
115:         }
116: 
117:         // 3. Child order (parents before children already exist), THEN props:
118:         //    the C++ layer attaches a widget to its final parent before its
119:         //    WIDTH/HEIGHT/ALIGNMENT arrive, so FILL/stretch resolve against the
120:         //    real parent (a Layout/positioner/window) instead of the create-time
121:         //    contentItem placeholder. The shared core's DELETE_NODE leaves a
122:         //    ghost in the parent's child list, so filter to live nodes.
123:         for &id in &order {
124:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
125:             let children: Vec<u32> = node
126:                 .children
127:                 .iter()
128:                 .copied()
129:                 .filter(|c| self.tree.nodes.contains_key(c))
130:                 .collect();
131:             let prev = self.sent_children.entry(id).or_default();
132:             cmds.extend(children_diff(id, prev, &children));
133:             *prev = children;
134:         }
135: 
136:         // 4. Roots are children of the pseudo-parent 0 (window contentItem).
137:         let mut roots: Vec<u32> = order
138:             .iter()
139:             .copied()
140:             .filter(|&id| self.tree.node(id).map_or(false, |n| n.parent.is_none()))
141:             .collect();
142:         roots.sort_unstable();
143:         let prev_roots = self.sent_children.entry(CONTENT_ITEM).or_default();
144:         cmds.extend(children_diff(CONTENT_ITEM, prev_roots, &roots));
145:         *prev_roots = roots;
146: 
147:         // 5. Text + property deltas (after the widget is attached to its final
148:         //    parent). On any property change we re-send the node's *complete*
149:         //    property set (preceded by RESET_NODE), so the C++ layer can reset
150:         //    removed properties to its renderer defaults.
151:         for &id in &order {
152:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
153:             let s = self.sent.get_mut(&id).unwrap();
154: 
155:             if s.text != node.text {
156:                 cmds.push(Command::set_text(id, node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or("")));
157:                 s.text = node.text.clone();
158:             }
159:             if node.date != s.date {
160:                 if let Some((days, millis)) = node.date {
161:                     cmds.push(Command::set_date(id, days, millis));
162:                 }
163:                 s.date = node.date;
164:             }
165:             let strings = string_props(node);
166:             if node.properties != s.props || strings != s.strings {
167:                 cmds.push(Command::reset_node(id));
168:                 // Emit numeric props in a deterministic order with VALUE last:
169:                 // Qt Quick clamps a control's `value` when `from`/`to` aren't
170:                 // configured yet, so min/max must land before the value.
171:                 let mut props: Vec<(u16, u32)> =
172:                     node.properties.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect();
173:                 // Order: TEXT_STYLE first (a base typography), then the rest
174:                 // (raw font modifiers override it), with VALUE last (Qt Quick
175:                 // clamps a control's value when from/to aren't configured yet).
176:                 use pathland_core::property_id::{TEXT_STYLE, VALUE};
177:                 props.sort_by_key(|(p, _)| (*p == VALUE, *p != TEXT_STYLE, *p));
178:                 for (prop, value) in &props {
179:                     let vt = value_type_for(*prop);
180:                     cmds.push(Command::set_property(id, *prop, vt, *value));
181:                 }
182:                 for (prop, value) in &strings {
183:                     cmds.push(Command::set_string_property(id, *prop, value));
184:                 }
185:                 s.props = node.properties.clone();
186:                 s.strings = strings;
187:             }
188:         }
189: 
190:         cmds
191:     }

193:     fn pre_order(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
194:         let mut order = Vec::new();
195:         let mut roots: Vec<u32> = self
196:             .tree
197:             .nodes
198:             .keys()
199:             .copied()
200:             .filter(|&id| self.tree.node(id).map_or(false, |n| n.parent.is_none()))
201:             .collect();
202:         roots.sort_unstable();
203:         for r in roots {
204:             self.walk(r, &mut order);
205:         }
206:         order
207:     }

209:     fn walk(&self, id: u32, out: &mut Vec<u32>) {
210:         // Guard against ghost children (a node deleted from `tree.nodes` but
211:         // still listed in a parent's `children` after DELETE_NODE).
212:         if !self.tree.nodes.contains_key(&id) {
213:             return;
214:         }
215:         out.push(id);
216:         if let Some(node) = self.tree.node(id) {
217:             for c in node.children.clone() {
218:                 self.walk(c, out);
219:             }
220:         }
221:     }
222: }

224: /// The string-valued properties a node sends to the C++ layer: its decoded
225: /// strings plus `LIST` properties serialized as CSV (today a `FIT_QUERY`
226: /// threshold table, which the Qt layer parses to measure a fit slot).
227: fn string_props(node: &HostNode) -> HashMap<u16, String> {
228:     let mut props = node.strings.clone();
229:     for (prop, values) in &node.lists {
230:         let csv = values
231:             .iter()
232:             .map(|v| v.to_string())
233:             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
234:             .join(",");
235:         props.insert(*prop, csv);
236:     }
237:     props
238: }

295: /// Minimal child-order delta: for each index where the old and new children
296: /// differ, remove the stale child and insert the new one at that index.
297: fn children_diff(parent: u32, prev: &[u32], next: &[u32]) -> Vec<Command> {
298:     let mut cmds = Vec::new();
299:     let len = prev.len().max(next.len());
300:     for i in 0..len {
301:         let old = prev.get(i).copied();
302:         let new = next.get(i).copied();
303:         if old == new {
304:             continue;
305:         }
306:         if let Some(c) = old {
307:             cmds.push(Command::remove_child(parent, c));
308:         }
309:         if let Some(c) = new {
310:             cmds.push(Command::insert_child(parent, c, i as u32));
311:         }
312:     }
313:     cmds
314: }

326:     /// One persistent engine + ring memory, so consecutive emits are **deltas**

329:         layout: MemoryLayout,
330:         mem: Vec<u8>,
331:         engine: Engine,
332:     }
333: 
334:     impl Harness {
335:         fn new() -> Self {
336:             let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
337:             let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
338:             init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
339:             Self {
340:                 layout,
341:                 mem,
342:                 engine: Engine::new(),
343:             }
344:         }

346:         /// Emit `root` (delta against the previous emit) and return the frame's
347:         /// slots + arena copied into owned buffers (`frame spans 0..len`).
348:         /// An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes (returns empty buffers).
349:         fn emit(&mut self, root: &Node) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
350:             let layout = self.layout;
351:             {
352:                 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
353:                 guest.begin_frame();
354:                 self.engine.emit(root, &mut guest).unwrap();
355:                 guest.end_frame();
356:             }
357:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
358:             let frames = host.frames();
359:             assert!(frames.len() <= 1, "at most one frame per emit");
360:             let Some(f) = frames.first() else {
361:                 return (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
362:             };
363:             let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(f.len() * 16);
364:             for op in f.opcodes() {
365:                 slots.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
366:             }
367:             let arena = f.arena().to_vec();
368:             (slots, arena)
369:         }
370:     }

375:         r.tree.apply_frame(&frame);

1: # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 20, 2026
4: 
5: The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
6: scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
7: Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
8: 
9: **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
10: - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
11:   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
12:   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
13:   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
14: - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
15:   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
16:   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
17:   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
18: 
19: ## Implemented
20: 
21: - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
22:   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
23:   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
24:   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
25:   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
26: - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
27:   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
28:   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
29:   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
30: - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
31:   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
32:   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
33:   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
34:   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
35:   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
36:   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
37:   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
38: - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
39:   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
40:   `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
41:   padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
42:   `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
43:   `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
44:   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
45:   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
46:   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
47:   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
48:   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
49:   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
50:   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
51:   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
52:   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
53:   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
54:   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
55:   FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
56:   `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
57:   property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
58:   value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
59:   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
60:   prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
61:   `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
62:   (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
63:   **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
64:   `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
65:   slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
66: - **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
67:   *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
68:   attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
69:   the create-time contentItem placeholder.
70: - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
71:   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
72:   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
73:   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
74:   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
75: - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
76:   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
77:   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
78:   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
79:   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
80:   `DELETE`.
81: - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
82:   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
83:   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
84: - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
85:   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
86:   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
87:   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
88:   init.
89: - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
90:   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
91:   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
92: - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
93:   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
94:   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
95: - **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
96:   `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
97:   sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
98:   `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
99:   sets it before `runRing`.
100: - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
101:   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
102:   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
103:   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
104:   a bare program name to Qt.
105: - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
106:   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
107:   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
108:   shared ring).
109: 
110: - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
111:   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
112:   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
113:   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
114:   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
115:   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
116:   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
117:   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
118:   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
119:   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
120:   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
121:   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
122:   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
123:   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
124:   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
125:   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
126:   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
127:   overflowing title).
128: 
129: - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
130:   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
131:   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
132:     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
133:     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
134:   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
135:     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
136:     (spec/MEDIA.md).
137:   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
138:     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
139:     parent/child edge).
140:   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
141:   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
142:     fills it.
143:   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
144:     the parent Grid.
145: - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
146:   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
147:   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
148: - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
149:   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
150:   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (only when it
151:   changes).
152: - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
153:   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
154: - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
155:   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
156:   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
157: - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
158:   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
159:   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
160:   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
161:   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
162:   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
163: - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
164:   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
165:     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
166:     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
167:     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
168:   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
169:     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
170:     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
171:     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
172:     native.
173:   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
174:     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
175:   - **Layout defaults**: cross-axis stretch (`align-items:stretch`) when no
176:     `ALIGNMENT` is set; `Spacer` expands on the main axis; `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
177:   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
178:     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
179:     offset shadow layer.
180: - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
181:   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
182:   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
183:   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
184:   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
185:   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
186:   echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
187:   the source lands.
188: - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
189:   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
190:   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
191:   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
192:   where applicable).
193: - **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
194:   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
195:   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
196:   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
197:   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
198: 
199: ## Not implemented / gaps
200: 
201: - **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
202:   `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
203: - **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
204:   is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
205:   dialog.
206: - **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
207:   controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
208:   layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
209: - **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
210:   symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
211: - **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
212:   `MultiEffect` shadow.
213: - **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
214:   text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and
215:   `DATE_CHANGED` are not yet reported. Hover/leave use `POINTER_MOVE` (the
216:   listener mask bit).
217: - **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
218:   `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
219:   defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
220:   `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly.
221: - The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
222:   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
223:   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
224: - The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` (the spec table is aspirational) —
225:   the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
226:   vehicle.
227: - `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
228:   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
229: - **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
230:   `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring`.
231: - Lazy views render eagerly.
232:

755: // The fit index for an allocated width: the largest candidate whose minWidth is
756: // <= width (thresholds ascending), clamped to the table (spec/PRIMITIVES.md).
757: int deriveFitIndex(const std::vector<double> &thresholds, double width) {
758:     if (thresholds.empty()) {
759:         return 0;
760:     }
761:     int index = 0;
762:     for (size_t i = 0; i < thresholds.size(); ++i) {
763:         if (thresholds[i] <= width) {
764:             index = static_cast<int>(i);
765:         } else {
766:             break;
767:         }
768:     }
769:     return index;
770: }

772: // Measure a fit slot and report FIT_CHANGED when the derived index changes.
773: void reportFit(uint32_t id, double width) {
774:     auto it = g.fit_queries.find(id);

780:     if (prev != g.fit_index.end() && prev->second == index) {
781:         return;
782:     }
783:     g.fit_index[id] = index;
784:     g.bridge->fitChanged(id, index);

883: // Pathland cross-axis alignment (0=Start,1=Center,2=End,3=Fill) applied to a
884: // stack's children via the Layout attached properties: Fill stretches the child
885: // on the stack's cross axis; Start/Center/End set the Layout alignment.
886: void applyStackAlignment(uint32_t parentId, QQuickItem *child) {
887:     if (!child) {
888:         return;
889:     }
890:     auto it = g.stack_align.find(parentId);
891:     if (it == g.stack_align.end()) {
892:         return;
893:     }
894:     const uint16_t comp = g.components[parentId];
895:     const bool vertical = comp == PL_COMP_VSTACK || comp == PL_COMP_LAZY_VSTACK;
896:     const float raw = f32(it->second);
897:     const int idx = (std::isfinite(raw) && std::floor(raw) == raw && raw >= 0.0f && raw <= 3.0f)
898:                         ? static_cast<int>(raw)
899:                         : static_cast<int>(it->second & 0xFF);
900:     QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child);
901:     if (!a) {
902:         return;
903:     }
904:     if (idx == 3) { // Fill -> stretch on the cross axis
905:         if (vertical) {
906:             a->setFillWidth(true);
907:         } else {
908:             a->setFillHeight(true);
909:         }
910:         return;
911:     }
912:     Qt::Alignment align;
913:     if (vertical) { // Column: cross axis is horizontal
914:         align = idx == 0 ? Qt::AlignLeft : (idx == 1 ? Qt::AlignHCenter : Qt::AlignRight);
915:     } else { // Row: cross axis is vertical
916:         align = idx == 0 ? Qt::AlignTop : (idx == 1 ? Qt::AlignVCenter : Qt::AlignBottom);
917:     }
918:     a->setAlignment(align);
919: }

924:         applyStackAlignment(parentId, findWidget(childId));

1805: void insertChild(uint32_t parentId, uint32_t childId, uint32_t index) {
1806:     QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
1807:     if (!child) {
1808:         return;
1809:     }
1810:     g.parents[childId] = parentId;
1811:     // Maintain the ordered structural mirror for every parent.
1812:     auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
1813:     siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
1814:     if (index == UINT32_MAX || index >= siblings.size()) {
1815:         siblings.push_back(childId);
1816:     } else {
1817:         siblings.insert(siblings.begin() + index, childId);
1818:     }
1819: 
1820:     if (isNonVisual(g.components[childId])) {
1821:         // Layout-transparent: it exists (owns playback), but no visual slot.
1822:         // CREATE_NODE parented it to the content item as a placeholder; detach.
1823:         if (QQuickItem *nv = findWidget(childId)) {
1824:             nv->setParentItem(nullptr);
1825:         }
1826:         return;
1827:     }
1828:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
1829:         rebuildPickerModel(parentId); // options drive the model, not the visual tree
1830:         return;
1831:     }
1832:     if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
1833:         reconcileNav(parentId); // destination subtree swap -> refresh/replace the top page
1834:         return; // the destination is placed by the nav adapter, not visually here
1835:     }
1836: 
1837:     // GRID_ROW (spec/PRIMITIVES.md): a row's cells are flattened into the parent
1838:     // Grid so columns align across rows. The row itself renders nothing.
1839:     if (g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_GRID_ROW &&
1840:         g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_GRID) {
1841:         g.grid_of[childId] = parentId;
1842:         if (QQuickItem *row = findWidget(childId)) {
1843:             QQuickItem *grid = findWidget(parentId);
1844:             for (QQuickItem *cell : row->childItems()) {
1845:                 cell->setParentItem(grid); // cells already present join the grid
1846:             }
1847:             row->setParentItem(nullptr);
1848:         }
1849:         return;
1850:     }
1851: 
1852:     // A GRID_ROW's cell attaches to the row's grid (flattened), at its global
1853:     // row-major cell index.
1854:     uint32_t visualParentId = parentId;
1855:     uint32_t visualIndex = index;
1856:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_GRID_ROW) {
1857:         auto git = g.grid_of.find(parentId);
1858:         if (git != g.grid_of.end()) {
1859:             visualParentId = git->second;
1860:             int n = 0;
1861:             for (uint32_t c : g.children_of[visualParentId]) {
1862:                 if (c == parentId) {
1863:                     break;
1864:                 }
1865:                 n += (g.components[c] == PL_COMP_GRID_ROW)
1866:                          ? static_cast<int>(g.children_of[c].size())
1867:                          : 1;
1868:             }
1869:             const auto &rowKids = g.children_of[parentId];
1870:             auto lit = std::find(rowKids.begin(), rowKids.end(), childId);
1871:             const int local = (lit == rowKids.end()) ? 0 : static_cast<int>(lit - rowKids.begin());
1872:             visualIndex = static_cast<uint32_t>(n + local);
1873:         }
1874:     }
1875: 
1876:     if (g.components[visualParentId] == PL_COMP_BUTTON && !isNonVisual(g.components[childId])) {
1877:         promoteComposite(visualParentId); // children => composite override mode
1878:     }
1879: 
1880:     QQuickItem *parent = findWidget(visualParentId);
1881:     if (!parent) {
1882:         return;
1883:     }
1884:     // Stacks attach children to their inner layout (so `Layout` stretch works);
1885:     // a ScrollView attaches to its contentItem (so content sizes/scrolls it).
1886:     QQuickItem *attach = parent;
1887:     if (isStackComponent(g.components[visualParentId]) || g.composite.count(visualParentId)) {
1888:         attach = layoutOf(parent);
1889:         if (!attach) {
1890:             attach = parent;
1891:         }
1892:     } else if (g.components[visualParentId] == PL_COMP_SCROLL) {
1893:         QVariant ci = parent->property("contentItem");
1894:         if (ci.isValid()) {
1895:             if (QQuickItem *c = ci.value<QQuickItem *>()) {
1896:                 attach = c;
1897:             }
1898:         }
1899:     }
1900: 
1901:     child->setParentItem(attach);
1902:     // Window content (pseudo-parent 0): roots fill the window (GTK's window
1903:     // child expands).
1904:     if (parentId == 0) {
1905:         QObject *anchors = child->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1906:         if (anchors) {
1907:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(g.root));
1908:         }
1909:     }
1910:     applyStackAlignment(parentId, child);
1911:     // Default stack alignment is stretch (CSS `align-items:stretch`): with no
1912:     // explicit ALIGNMENT, a child fills the container's cross axis.
1913:     if (isContainer(visualParentId) && isLayout(attach) &&
1914:         !g.stack_align.count(visualParentId)) {
1915:         if (QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child)) {
1916:             if (isVerticalContainer(visualParentId)) {
1917:                 a->setFillWidth(true);
1918:             } else {
1919:                 a->setFillHeight(true);
1920:             }
1921:         }
1922:     }
1923:     // A Spacer expands along the container's main axis.
1924:     if (g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_SPACER && isContainer(visualParentId) &&
1925:         isLayout(attach)) {
1926:         if (QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child)) {
1927:             if (isVerticalContainer(visualParentId)) {
1928:                 a->setFillHeight(true);
1929:             } else {
1930:                 a->setFillWidth(true);
1931:             }
1932:         }
1933:     }
1934:     // A ScrollView fills its parent by default (GTK: halign/valign = Fill), so a
1935:     // scroll content area stretches instead of collapsing to its content. A
1936:     // SIZE_THAT_FITS slot is likewise greedy on both axes (spec/LAYOUT.md).
1937:     if (g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_SCROLL ||
1938:         g.components[childId] == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
1939:         if (isLayout(attach)) {
1940:             QQuickLayoutAttached *a = layoutAttached(child);
1941:             if (a) {
1942:                 a->setFillWidth(true);
1943:                 a->setFillHeight(true);
1944:             }
1945:         } else if (!isPositioner(attach)) {
1946:             QObject *anchors = child->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1947:             if (anchors) {
1948:                 anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(attach));
1949:             }
1950:         }
1951:     }
1952:     // Inherit a container's foreground color (CSS `color` inheritance).
1953:     if (isTextual(child) && !g.fg_own.count(childId)) {
1954:         uint32_t color = 0;
1955:         if (inheritedForeground(childId, &color)) {
1956:             child->setProperty("color", QColor::fromRgba(color));
1957:         }
1958:     }
1959:     // A fit slot's one selected child occupies the whole slot.
1960:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
1961:         QObject *anchors = child->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
1962:         if (anchors) {
1963:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(attach));
1964:         }
1965:     }
1966:     flushFill(child, attach);
1967:     if (visualIndex == UINT32_MAX) {
1968:         return; // append (already last)
1969:     }
1970:     QList<QQuickItem *> siblingsList = attach->childItems();
1971:     siblingsList.removeAll(child);
1972:     if (static_cast<int>(visualIndex) < siblingsList.size()) {
1973:         QQuickItem *after = siblingsList.at(static_cast<int>(visualIndex));
1974:         if (after != child) {
1975:             child->stackBefore(after);
1976:         }
1977:     }
1978: }

2024: // Native back: Escape is a platform back request (global, never node-keyed),
2025: // matching the GTK renderer's window-level key controller. BackSpace is
2026: // deferred (needs text-focus detection).
2027: class KeyFilter : public QObject {
2028: public:
2029:     using QObject::QObject;
2030: protected:
2031:     bool eventFilter(QObject *obj, QEvent *ev) override {
2032:         if (ev->type() != QEvent::KeyPress && ev->type() != QEvent::KeyRelease) {
2033:             return QObject::eventFilter(obj, ev);
2034:         }
2035:         auto *ke = static_cast<QKeyEvent *>(ev);
2036:         const bool down = ev->type() == QEvent::KeyPress;
2037:         // Escape is always native back (global, never node-keyed).
2038:         if (down && ke->key() == Qt::Key_Escape) {
2039:             if (g.bridge) {
2040:                 g.bridge->navigateBack();
2041:             }
2042:             return true;
2043:         }
2044:         // BackSpace is native back unless a text input owns the key.
2045:         if (down && ke->key() == Qt::Key_Backspace && !isTextInput(g.focused_component)) {
2046:             if (g.bridge) {
2047:                 g.bridge->navigateBack();
2048:             }
2049:             return true;
2050:         }
2051:         // Report KEY_DOWN/KEY_UP for the focused node (gated by its listener bits
2052:         // inside the Bridge); the event still reaches the focused control.
2053:         if (g.focused_id != 0 && g.bridge) {
2054:             g.bridge->key(g.focused_id, ke->key(), modifierMask(ke->modifiers()),
2055:                           ke->isAutoRepeat(), down);
2056:         }
2057:         return QObject::eventFilter(obj, ev);
2058:     }
2059: };

2156: void pathland_qt_layer_apply(const PathlandQtCommand *cmds, uint32_t count) {
2157:     if (!g.initialized || !cmds || count == 0) {
2158:         return;
2159:     }
2160:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
2161:         const PathlandQtCommand &c = cmds[i];
2162:         switch (c.kind) {
2163:         case PLQT_CREATE_NODE: {
2164:             const uint16_t component = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
2165:             QQuickItem *item = createComponent(g.engine, g.root, qmlFor(component, c.a).toUtf8());
2166:             if (item) {
2167:                 g.widgets[c.a] = item;
2168:                 g.components[c.a] = component;
2169:                 if (component == PL_COMP_SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
2170:                     const uint32_t id = c.a;
2171:                     QObject::connect(item, &QQuickItem::widthChanged, item,
2172:                                      [id, item]() { reportFit(id, item->width()); });
2173:                 }
2174:                 if (isTextInput(component)) {
2175:                     const uint32_t id = c.a;
2176:                     QObject::connect(item, &QQuickItem::activeFocusChanged, item, [id, item]() {
2177:                         const bool focused = item->hasActiveFocus();
2178:                         if (focused) {
2179:                             g.focused_id = id;
2180:                             g.focused_component = g.components[id];
2181:                         } else if (g.focused_id == id) {
2182:                             g.focused_id = 0;
2183:                             g.focused_component = 0;
2184:                         }
2185:                         if (g.bridge) {
2186:                             g.bridge->focusChanged(id, focused);
2187:                             g.bridge->editingChanged(id, focused);
2188:                         }
2189:                     });
2190:                 }
2191:             }
2192:             break;
2193:         }
2194:         case PLQT_DELETE_NODE:
2195:             deleteNode(c.a);
2196:             break;
2197:         case PLQT_INSERT_CHILD:
2198:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c);
2199:             break;
2200:         case PLQT_REMOVE_CHILD: {
2201:             const uint32_t parentId = c.a;
2202:             const uint32_t childId = c.b;
2203:             g.parents.erase(childId);
2204:             auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
2205:             siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
2206:             if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
2207:                 rebuildPickerModel(parentId);
2208:             } else if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
2209:                 reconcileNav(parentId);
2210:             } else {
2211:                 QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
2212:                 if (child) {
2213:                     child->setParentItem(nullptr); // keep alive (may be reinserted)
2214:                 }
2215:             }
2216:             break;
2217:         }
2218:         case PLQT_MOVE_CHILD:
2219:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c); // reorder == reinsert at index
2220:             break;
2221:         case PLQT_SET_TEXT: {
2222:             QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a);
2223:             if (item && c.str) {
2224:                 g.suppress = true;
2225:                 item->setProperty("text", QString::fromUtf8(c.str, static_cast<int>(c.str_len)));
2226:                 g.suppress = false;
2227:             }
2228:             // A picker option's label feeds its parent's ComboBox model.
2229:             auto pit = g.parents.find(c.a);
2230:             if (pit != g.parents.end() && g.components[pit->second] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
2231:                 rebuildPickerModel(pit->second);
2232:             }
2233:             // Record for the test hook.
2234:             if (c.str && c.str_len > 0) {
2235:                 const uint32_t n = c.str_len < sizeof(g.last_text) - 1 ? c.str_len
2236:                                                                        : sizeof(g.last_text) - 1;
2237:                 std::memcpy(g.last_text, c.str, n);
2238:                 g.last_text[n] = '\0';
2239:                 g.last_text_len = n;
2240:             }
2241:             break;
2242:         }
2243:         case PLQT_SET_PROPERTY: {
2244:             const uint16_t prop = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
2245:             const uint8_t vt = static_cast<uint8_t>((c.b >> 16) & 0xFF);
2246:             g.suppress = true;
2247:             applyProperty(c.a, prop, vt, c.c);
2248:             g.suppress = false;
2249:             break;
2250:         }
2251:         case PLQT_SET_STRING_PROPERTY:
2252:             g.suppress = true;
2253:             applyStringProperty(c.a, static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b), c.str, c.str_len);
2254:             g.suppress = false;
2255:             break;
2256:         case PLQT_RESET_NODE:
2257:             resetNode(c.a);
2258:             break;
2259:         case PLQT_SET_SCHEME:
2260:             break; // MVP: scheme handling is a follow-up
2261:         case PLQT_SET_DATE: {
2262:             // A DATE_PICKER value: days since the Unix epoch + millis of day.
2263:             // The renderer owns the formatting (QML approximation of a picker).
2264:             if (QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a)) {
2265:                 const qint64 days = static_cast<int32_t>(c.b);
2266:                 const QDate date = QDate(1970, 1, 1).addDays(days);
2267:                 QString text = date.toString(QStringLiteral("yyyy-MM-dd"));
2268:                 const int millis = static_cast<int>(c.c);
2269:                 if (millis > 0) {
2270:                     const int hours = millis / 3'600'000;
2271:                     const int minutes = (millis / 60'000) % 60;
2272:                     text += QStringLiteral(" %1:%2")
2273:                                 .arg(hours, 2, 10, QChar('0'))
2274:                                 .arg(minutes, 2, 10, QChar('0'));
2275:                 }
2276:                 g.suppress = true;
2277:                 item->setProperty("text", text);
2278:                 g.suppress = false;
2279:             }
2280:             break;
2281:         }
2282:         }
2283:     }
2284:     g.apply_count += count;
2285: }

2: //!
3: //! Mirrors `pathland-render-gtk`'s `capi.rs`:
4: //! - `pathland_qt_run(host, on_event)` — pump a `pathland-view-native`
5: //!   `NativeHost`'s ring in-process.
6: //! - `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` — pump a
7: //!   `libpathland_core` ring borrowed in-process (the route for hosts that
8: //!   emit opcodes themselves, e.g. the Java DSL's `RingOpcodeSink`).
9: //!
10: //! Both block until the Qt event loop exits and pass a bare program name to
11: //! Qt (the process argv belongs to the embedding host — e.g. a JVM's `-cp` /
12: //! `-D` flags — and must not be parsed as Qt options).

24: /// A `Pump` over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost` owned by the foreign host.
25: struct NativeHostHandle(*mut NativeHost);

27: impl Pump for NativeHostHandle {
28:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
29:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); the host must not destroy
30:         // the host until `pathland_qt_run` returns.
31:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
32:     }
33: 
34:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
35:         // SAFETY: as above.
36:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
37:     }
38: }

40: /// A `Pump` over a `libpathland_core` `RingTransport` borrowed from the foreign
41: /// host. Same contract as [`NativeHostHandle`].
42: struct CoreRingHandle(*mut RingTransport);
43: 
44: impl Pump for CoreRingHandle {
45:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
46:         // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); the ring outlives the call.
47:         unsafe { FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *self.0) }
48:     }
49: 
50:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
51:         // SAFETY: as above.
52:         unsafe { DriverTransport::send_input(&mut *self.0, event) }
53:     }

61: /// the host then drains the event ring via `pathland_native_drain_events` and
62: /// may re-enter `pathland_native_*` to update the tree and re-emit.

## Plan: HStack/VStack layout tests for the Qt renderer

### What I found

The Qt renderer is split: Rust (`renderer.rs` delta diff + `ffi.rs` FFI boundary) → C++ (`qt_layer.cpp` QML scene). VStack renders as a wrapper `Item` holding a `ColumnLayout`; HStack holds a `RowLayout`. Existing live-scene tests (`fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`, `default_stack_stretch_and_spacer`, `renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`) already assert fill/preferred/spacing wiring, but **none assert actual child geometry** — i.e. that VStack children stack vertically and HStack children flow horizontally.

The C++ test hooks already expose `pathland_qt_layer_widget_size` (width/height) and `pathland_qt_layer_render_once` (force a synchronous layout pass), but **there is no position (x/y) hook**, so "laid out correctly" can't yet be asserted.

### Changes

**1. Add a position test hook** (needed to assert geometry):
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp` — add `pathland_qt_layer_widget_position(uint32_t id, uint32_t which)` returning `item->x()` (which==0) / `item->y()` (which==1), next to `pathland_qt_layer_widget_size`.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/pathland_qt.h` — declare it.
- `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/ffi.rs` — add the matching `extern "C"` declaration.

**2. Add two tests** in `ffi.rs` `mod tests` (using the existing `with_qt` harness + `pathland_qt_layer_render_once`, hand-built command batches like `fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`, with fixed main-axis sizes for deterministic geometry):

- `vstack_lays_out_children_vertically` — VSTACK(1) with two TEXT children (fixed `HEIGHT`=50) + `SPACING`=10:
  - `y(2) == 0`, `y(3) ≈ y(2) + h(2) + 10` (second child below the first)
  - `x(2) == x(3)` (default cross-axis stretch aligns left)
  - gap ≈ spacing (assert with a small epsilon, e.g. 0.5)
- `hstack_lays_out_children_horizontally` — HSTACK(1) with two TEXT children (fixed `WIDTH`=100) + `SPACING`=10:
  - `x(2) == 0`, `x(3) ≈ x(2) + w(2) + 10` (second child to the right)
  - `y(2) == y(3)` (default cross-axis stretch aligns top)
  - gap ≈ spacing

**3. Update `status.md`** — add the two tests to the "Verified by" list.

**4. Verify** — `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; runs offscreen).

### Notes / assumptions
- I'll use hand-built `Command` batches (matching the existing layout tests) rather than the DSL for precise, deterministic geometry. I can add a DSL-driven end-to-end variant too if you'd prefer the tests exercise the full DSL→engine→frame→renderer path.
- Root stacks are anchored to fill the 420×220 window; `render_once()` forces the Qt Quick Layouts pass so `x()`/`y()`/`width()`/`height()` are populated before asserting.

Want me to proceed with hand-built commands only, or also add a DSL end-to-end test for each?

Done. Added two live-scene layout tests plus the position test hook they need.

**Changes**
- `src/qt/qt_layer.cpp:2422` — new `pathland_qt_layer_widget_position(id, which)` test hook (x/y).
- `src/qt/pathland_qt.h:141` — declaration.

- `src/ffi.rs:507` — `vstack_lays_out_children_vertically` and `hstack_lays_out_children_horizontally`: build a fixed-size stack inside a `ZStack`, force a layout pass via `pathland_qt_layer_render_once`, then assert children stack on the main axis in order, stay cross-axis aligned, and the `SPACING` gap rests between them.
- `status.md` — noted the new coverage.

**Result:** `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` → 38 passed, 0 failed.

Note: each stack is sized to exact content (VStack `2×50+10`, HStack `2×100+10`) because a Qt `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout` that fills extra space expands its rows/cells and centers non-filling items — sizing to content keeps the spacing gap directly observable.
